title: Ὄρνις καὶ χελιδών
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 286. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ὄρνις ὄφεως ὠὰ εὑροῦσα, ταῦτα ἐπιμελῶς ἐθέρμαινε καὶ μετὰ τὸ θερμᾶναι ἐξεκόλαψε.
sentences.tr: Ornis opheōs ōa heurousa, tauta epimelōs ethermaine kai meta to thermanai exekolapse.
sentences.l: A hen, having found a snake's eggs, kept warming them carefully and after the warming hatched them out.
sentences.i: A hen found a snake's eggs and brooded over them carefully, and when she had warmed them through she hatched them out.
sentences.n: ὄρνις covers both 'bird' generally and 'hen' in particular; the brooding and hatching fix the sense here, whereas at fable 283 the same noun is simply 'birds'. μετὰ τὸ θερμᾶναι is the articular infinitive — the infinitive turned into a noun by the article, so that a preposition can govern it: 'after the warming'.

sentences.t: Χελιδὼν δὲ θεασαμένη αὐτὴν ἔφη· « Ὦ ματαία, τί ταῦτα ἀνατρέφεις ἅπερ, ἂν αὐξηθῇ, ἀπὸ σοῦ πρώτης τοῦ ἀδικεῖν ἄρξεται ; »
sentences.tr: Chelidōn de theasamenē autēn ephē· « Ō mataia, ti tauta anatrepheis haper, an auxēthēi, apo sou prōtēs tou adikein arxetai ; »
sentences.l: And a swallow, having watched her, said: « O foolish creature, why do you rear these things, which, if they grow, will begin their wrong-doing from you first? »
sentences.i: And a swallow watched her and said: « You foolish creature, why are you rearing these? Once they are grown, you are the first they will wrong. »
sentences.n: ἀπὸ σοῦ πρώτης — the adjective agrees with 'you' where English would use an adverb, 'from you as the first'; the feminine ending keeps the hen in view. ἄρξεται τοῦ ἀδικεῖν puts the articular infinitive in the genitive after ἄρχομαι, 'make a beginning of wronging'. The mark closing the question is the Greek semicolon, and the space before it is Chambry's printing-house habit.

sentences.t: Οὕτως ἀτιθάσσευτός ἐστιν ἡ πονηρία, κἂν τὰ μάλιστα εὐεργετῆται.
sentences.tr: Houtōs atithasseutos estin hē ponēria, kan ta malista euergetētai.
sentences.l: So untameable is wickedness, even if it is treated with the utmost kindness.
sentences.n: ἀτιθάσσευτος is built on the same root as the τιθασσός, the 'tame' partridge of fable 285 and the tame doves of fable 282 — the whole run of fables is about what can and cannot be domesticated. κἂν is καὶ ἐάν run together, and τὰ μάλιστα is the adverbial accusative 'to the utmost', as at fable 284.
